title: Parsl+CWL: Towards Combining the Python and CWL Ecosystems
problem: CWL and Parsl ecosystems operate independently, requiring users to choose between CWL's portability and standardization or Parsl's Python integration and diverse execution environment support. Integration between these complementary systems has not been developed.
motivation: Unified workflow development combining both ecosystems enables flexible computational workflows that benefit from CWL's portability and Parsl's Python-native execution across diverse HPC environments.
method: The system bridges CWL and Parsl by automatically converting CWL CommandLineTool definitions (standardized descriptions of command-line tools) into Parsl apps (Python-based workflow components), so existing CWL workflows can run as part of Python code. It also provides a Parsl runner that executes CWL CommandLineTool definitions directly, without conversion, giving users flexibility in workflow style. As a proof-of-concept, it allows Python code to be embedded directly in CWL workflows. Performance is evaluated using image-processing workflows.
key_novelty: CWL CommandLineTool definitions can be converted into Parsl apps, enabling standard CWL workflows to run directly within Python code.
contributions: Method to convert CWL CommandLineTool definitions into Parsl apps
Parsl runner for direct execution of CWL CommandLineTool
Proof-of-concept extension supporting inline Python in CWL workflows

metrics.speedup: Compared across CWL runners; specific values not provided in abstract

limitations: Proof-of-concept status for Python extension indicates preliminary maturity; broader deployment considerations and scalability limits not discussed.
